group_a_pages.ground_truth_source: curl -L --compressed https://www.anthropic.com/pricing, grepped raw HTML for $-prices (Webflow data-plan attributes)

runs.question: What is the name and monthly price (annual billing) of the cheapest paid individual plan?

returned_data.title: Pricing
returned_data.summary: Anthropic's Claude subscription plans overview showing three tiers: Free, Pro, and Max.

runs.note: success=true but the direct answer requested is null. Ground truth ($17/mo Pro, annual) is present as literal visible text in the raw static HTML inside Webflow pricing-card divs, but the tier-1 static content extraction evidently strips/deprioritizes this structured widget markup before it reaches the LLM, so the model correctly declined to guess (no hallucination) but also did not escalate to tier 2 (rendered DOM) to recover the missing number. This is a real gap: 'success: true' with a null answer is a soft failure that a caller could mistake for a validated non-answer.

Plan name correct ('Pro'). Price field null for the same extraction-gap reason as the page_info run. No hallucinated price was fabricated -- pipeline behaved safely, just incompletely, and did not escalate tiers to fill the gap.

group_b_guardrails.verdict: pass -- pipeline escalated through tiers up to tier 4 vision (tried haiku then sonnet, 2 attempts total, no infinite retry loop) and then failed cleanly with a non-zero exit code, correctly distinguishing a genuine pipeline error from a policy-based refusal.

top_observations: Guardrails are solid: blocked_robots and auth_required are both reachable via realistic URLs, are cleanly distinguishable from each other (robots-level short-circuit with 0 attempts vs. render-then-detect with 1 attempt), never fabricate data, and both correctly exit 0 (refusal) while only a genuine unreachable-host error exits 1 -- with bounded retries (2 attempts across tiers/models), not a retry loop.

No hallucination was observed anywhere in Group A: on every field the model either returned a value that matched ground truth exactly or returned null. This is the encouraging finding -- the model behaves safely, preferring null/omission over invention.

The concerning finding is the inverse failure mode: on the Anthropic pricing page, tier-1 static content extraction silently drops price text that lives inside heavily-classed Webflow div markup, causing 'success: true' with a null value for the exact field requested. The pipeline does not detect 'field explicitly asked for came back null' as a signal to escalate to tier 2 (rendered) -- it accepts tier 1 as done. This means fields/pricing extraction on JS-templated marketing sites can silently under-deliver while reporting success.

Similarly on python.org/about, page_info answered a question that was not the one asked (missed the literal hero tagline in favor of generic community/license facts) while still reporting status ok -- suggests the summarization step doesn't verify it addressed the specific --question before returning.
